A1.justification: Both PDFs describe the same GRE Suite study. All 22 pages of each version, including Appendices A–E, equations, figures, and tables, support reliable comparison.

before.justification: v1 reports original GRE benchmark evaluations, training-stage ablations, and qualitative predictions, including additional results in Appendix C.

after.justification: v3 retains the original benchmark evaluations, ablations, and appendix results. Retained experimental outcomes qualify as original empirical results.

M1.justification: The cold-start supervised fine-tuning, two-stage GRPO training, accuracy and format rewards, and inference prompts are unchanged in Section 3 and Figures 11–12.

E1.justification: Both versions retain MP-16/MP16-Pro-derived training data and evaluations on Im2GPS3k, GWS15k, GREval-Bench, and Google StreetView. Newly cited datasets are discussed as related work, without added training or evaluation coverage.

E2.justification: Comparator membership is unchanged in Tables 2–4 and 6–7 and the qualitative comparisons. Newly cited approaches such as GAGA, GeoReasoner, and SeekWorld are not added to the reported comparisons.

E3.justification: Training proportions, sample-count descriptions, model sizes, budgets, distance thresholds, and the CoT-quality metric are unchanged. The new attribution for reasoning-step partitioning does not establish a revised evaluation procedure.

E4.justification: Table 4 retains the same cold-start and RL-stage ablations. The refinement example and qualitative cases in Figures 10 and 13–15 are also unchanged; no new robustness or sensitivity analysis appears.

E5.justification: Neither version reports experimental random seeds, repeated-run counts, confidence intervals, error bars, or statistical significance tests. Uncertainty-reporting practices remain unchanged.

E6.justification: Numerical results in Tables 2–4 and 6–7 and the displayed qualitative predictions are unchanged after matching relocated content. For example, GRE's Im2GPS3k city accuracy remains 35.3% and its GREval-Bench CoT-quality score remains 59.54.

T1.justification: Equations 1–6 retain the same GRPO objectives, geodesic distance, reward definitions, and CoT-quality formula. No formal assumptions, derivations, or proofs are added or revised.

C1.justification: The abstract, introduction's contribution list, and conclusion retain the same GRE training, GRE30K dataset, GREval-Bench, and performance claims. Added motivation for reasoning-quality evaluation reiterates an existing rationale.

C2.justification: Appendix B.1 removes the assertion that giving o3 ground-truth coordinates yields more accurate rationales than instruction-only prompting, while retaining that procedure. This narrows its explanatory justification; Appendix D's limitations and future-work discussion are unchanged.

D1.justification: Section 4 newly specifies that reasoning-step categories and partitioning follow MME-CoT, clarifying the reference procedure for annotation. Prompts, filtering instructions, hyperparameters, hardware disclosures, and the planned code/data release remain unchanged.

R1.justification: v3 adds focused discussion of diffusion-based and reasoning-based geolocation, including Around the World in 80 Timesteps, GAGA, GeoReasoner, and SeekWorld. It also acknowledges prior datasets and CoT-evaluation work and explicitly attributes step categorization to MME-CoT, while retaining the broader research framing.

P1.justification: There are localized additions and rewrites in the introduction, related work, and Appendix B.1, plus updated affiliations/contact information and bibliography cleanup. The section hierarchy and most prose remain unchanged.

P2.justification: All fifteen figures and seven tables are retained. Layout changes relocate Table 2 from page 8 to 9, Figure 11 from page 19 to 18, and Tables 6–7 from page 20 to 19, with associated text reflow.

improvement.justification: v3 improves scholarly positioning by acknowledging closely related geolocation approaches and explicitly crediting the source of its reasoning-step evaluation structure. Appendix B.1 also drops a comparative rationale-quality assertion without a reported supporting comparison. These are useful, limited improvements; the method, empirical evidence, and principal limitations remain unchanged.
